title: Chapter 1
content:
"Take a deep, slow breath... Hold it for a moment, and clear your mind."

In front of a floor-to-ceiling glass window, Jakyeong unrolled his yoga mat. Bare-chested, he crossed his legs into a full lotus. With every rise and fall of his chest, the coiled serpent tattooed across his right shoulder seemed to writhe, its jaws gaping open. Outside, the midday heat hovered near a stifling 100 degrees, but inside Jakyeong’s apartment, the air conditioning held a chill so sharp it demanded long sleeves.

Soft, ambient meditation music drifted continuously from the speakers.

"Release the anger, the hatred, every toxic emotion lingering in your heart... Let it all float away."

Heavy footsteps echoed from the entryway. Jakyeong didn't flinch. A slow, rhythmic tread crossed the room, followed by the soft thud of something hitting the floor beside him. Only then did he crack his eyes open to glance sideways.

It was a newspaper, hot off the presses from Thailand that very morning. Front-page news: a massive photo of the man Jakyeong had put down last night. Above him, a slow, mocking round of applause broke the quiet. Jakyeong’s eyes tracked up from the headline to the tall, heavily built man standing over him. Wang Han. A mainland Chinese fixer, and as close to a brother as Jakyeong had in this line of work.

"Classic," Wang Han said, shaking his head with a grin. "Flawless as always."

The dead man was Yang Yang, a Chinese underworld figure making his fortune in underage prostitution and organ trafficking out of Thailand. That morning, he’d been found fully nude on a luxury hotel bed with a single hole through his left chest. A 7.62mm round, fired from a building across the street, had punched straight through the glass and pierced his heart with surgical precision.

"Everyone's celebrating," Wang Han chuckled. "Good riddance, honestly. Guy had it coming a thousand times over."

Jakyeong couldn't care less how vile the target was. A contract was a contract. You take the job, you take the life, you take the cash. Simple.

"Where's the money?"

The smirk vanished from Wang Han's lips.

"Where’s the rest of the payment?" Jakyeong repeated, his brows knitting as he looked at Wang Han’s empty hands. All he’d brought was a folded newspaper. By their schedule, he should have been holding a duffel packed with three hundred thousand dollars in crisp, untraceable cash.

Wang Han hesitated, pointing a reluctant thumb toward the dining table behind him. Sitting on the previously bare surface was a brown paper fast-food bag.

"Let's eat first. You haven't had breakfast yet, right?" Wang Han walked over, pulled out a burger, and jammed a straw into a large cup of soda. The table was built for two—cozy, neat. He carefully peeled back the paper wrapper to make it easy to eat, but Jakyeong just sat there on his mat, staring him down.

Wang Han forced a tight smile. "He said he’ll have it soon."

Before the sentence fully landed, Jakyeong was already on his feet. His brow was deeply furrowed, his entire posture radiating cold displeasure. Without a word, he turned away from the table and headed straight for the bedroom.

Damn it. Wang Han squeezed his eyes shut in frustration and hurried after him.

Inside, Jakyeong was casually browsing through his hung shirts. He pulled out a Hawaiian button-down printed with vibrant red flowers—a cheap night-market steal he’d been oddly proud of a few days back. As he buttoned it up, a slight, almost eager expression touched his face. It was the exact look he got right before he went out to kill someone.

"Where are you going?"

"To collect."

"Just calm down and listen to me for a second," Wang Han pleaded, stepping into his path. "Something came up on his end."

Jakyeong ignored him, sliding open the top drawer of his nightstand. A sleek silver Beretta gleamed in the light.

"I'm listening. Speak."

Instead of the gun, though, Jakyeong reached for the wristwatch laying beside it. Calling it a watch was a stretch; it was effectively a localized yield device. One press of a button wouldn't level a skyscraper, but it would easily vaporize anything within a few yards of the blast.

Wang Han’s face hardened. "I'll go handle it tomorrow."

"No. I'm getting it myself. Today."

"Why make it a whole scene? Look, forget it—I'll go right now. Just stay here."

Jakyeong was already brushing past him toward the front door. Wang Han stood frozen, a pit sinking in his stomach as he recalled the client’s face from this morning. Dmitri—a Russian-Chinese boss running a notorious syndicate. A man who usually kept his word down to the minute had suddenly pushed the final payout back by three days. That wasn't just an inconvenience; it meant something in the pipeline had broken. And Jakyeong wasn't the type to tolerate broken promises. He was the kind of psychopath who’d calculate interest on a late payment down to the exact second.

At the front door, Jakyeong paused and looked back over his shoulder.

"Don't follow me."

"Why not?"

"Stay here and hunt down the cockroach."

Wang Han blinked, completely thrown off. "The what?"

"I'm pretty sure I saw a roach this morning. About this big." Jakyeong held his thumb and forefinger a terrifying distance apart, shuddering visibly as he wiped his palms on his trousers. "Disgusting. Absolutely not."

Wang Han knew how much Jakyeong loathed roaches. The ones in Southeast Asia didn't just crawl—they were big enough to practically walk on two legs. But still...

"Are you seriously talking about bugs right now?!"

"To me, it's just as important as getting paid," Jakyeong said deadseriously. "I will never co-exist with those things. And make sure you actually crush it. Don't just spray it like last time. If it shows its face again, I won't be able to sleep."

He turned the door handle, pausing one last time.

"...Assuming I come back alive, of course."

He dropped the line about his potential death like it was a casual punchline, stepped out, and let the door click shut.

Left alone, Wang Han rubbed a hand over his face, a deep groan rasping from his throat. Trying to hold that kid back was like trying to stop a bullet mid-flight. He just prayed he wouldn't be reading Jakyeong’s obituary in tomorrow’s paper.

A private chef laid out a tender filet mignon, and Dmitri picked up his silver cutlery, carving into the meat with practiced elegance. With every subtle slice, the oversized gem on his ring caught the light. Surrounding him, heavily armed guards carrying submachine guns stood at the ready, while handlers patrolled the perimeter with snarling attack dogs.

Dmitri glanced at the newspaper resting to his left. Front page, bold print: Yang Yang—his long-time thorn in the side—was officially dead. As a broad smile spread across Dmitri's face, dark red juices pooled onto the stark white porcelain plate.

He lifted a piece to his mouth, savoring the rich flavor. With his rival out of the picture, an immense weight felt lifted from his chest. He dabbed the corner of his lips with a linen napkin—and then, a deafening CRASH shattered the afternoon quiet at the main gate.

Dmitri stopped chewing.

The roaring whine of a high-performance engine ripped through the air as a sleek black Jaguar tore across the manicured estate. The guards reacted instantly, scrambling into formation with weapons raised. Right in front of Dmitri’s dining table, the Jaguar whipped sideways, tires shrieking as it skidded to a dead stop.

Dmitri’s face contorted as he took in the ruined, tire-plowed turf of his pristine lawn. He spat his half-chewed steak onto the plate just as the driver’s door swung open.

Blaring, ear-splitting music spilled out from the cabin. A man stepped out onto the gravel wearing a garish, bright floral shirt and dark sunglasses. The guards leveled their barrels at him as one.

Jakyeong walked right past the wall of loaded guns as if they were invisible. He pulled out the chair across from Dmitri and dropped into it, making himself right at home.

"Care to join me?" Dmitri asked smoothly.

Jakyeong took off his sunglasses and tossed them onto the tablecloth. "Keep the food. Just give me my money."

His sharp brown eyes gleamed with a cold, predatory light. "Look at you. Smiling like a man whose biggest problem just vanished overnight."

"It did—until a minute ago," Dmitri replied, leaning back. "I was enjoying a peaceful meal until you ruined it."

"If you paid on time, I wouldn't be here. Right now, your late fee is ticking up by the second."

Dmitri scoffed, picking his knife and fork back up to cut another piece of meat. Jakyeong casually slid a hand into his trouser pocket. Instantly, a dozen gun barrels clicked, locking onto his head.

Jakyeong let out a dry chuckle. Unbothered, he pulled out a pack of cigarettes and a silver Zippo.

"Touchy, aren't we?"

He flicked the lighter, lit the tip, and leaned back comfortably into the chair.

"You've got three minutes. Or I take your head as the final payment."

The guards stood on razor-thin edge, eyes glued to the glowing ember of the cigarette as it slowly burned down to ash. If the kid made one wrong move, they were ordered to turn him into Swiss cheese. But nobody dared pull a trigger prematurely. No one who had ever crossed Jakyeong lived to brag about it. He was a ghost with guns and explosives alike—there was no telling what kind of dead-man's trap he had rigged on his person.

Taking one last drag, Jakyeong casually flicked the spent butt. It arced through the air and landed with perfect precision right on top of the rare steak on Dmitri's plate.

"Looks a little pink," Jakyeong murmured softly. "Thought I'd help you cook it."

The corner of Dmitri’s mouth twitched upward into a dark grin. "This is why I like you, kid. You don't fear a damn thing."

Jakyeong didn't smile back. He just glanced down at his wrist.

"Fifteen seconds."

"Not to mention your talent," Dmitri continued.

"Ten seconds. Any last words?"

"Which brings me to my next offer..."

"Five."

"...Go to Korea and eliminate a target for me. It's a VIP. I'll pay ten times your usual rate."
